_comment: The Outlaw Lord's beats (Expansion 6 D.3): his moves (an omen, a warning nailed to your door, a test on the road) and the steps' own (watching the loading for the man who sells the days, the choice between a parley and breaking the gang, the hideout's door with its parley).

text: {omen}
The road bends, and there it is. {omen}
You stop the party with a raised hand. {omen}
{gang} knows you are on the road. It wants you to know it knows.
Somebody has watched you from the ridge since morning. {gang} wants you to see that it has.
Whoever left this left it for you, and is not far away.
In the morning there is a knife in your door, driven into the wood to the hilt, and a paper under it. Nobody in the place heard a thing, or nobody will say.
You wake to find a knife driven into the post by your bed, to the hilt, with a paper folded round the blade. Whoever did it came and went without a sound.
There is a knife in the wood within reach of where you slept, and a paper under it. It was done in the night, and nobody will own to hearing it.

label: Pull the knife out and keep it.
result: It is a good knife, better than a robber should own. Somebody is being paid well.
The knife comes out with a little work. It is oiled and balanced, and not at all what a common robber carries.

label: Ask who came in the night.
result: The pot-boy will not meet your eye, and then he does. "A man from town," he whispers. "Not one of them. One of us."
In the end somebody tells you, without being asked twice: whoever it was knew the place, and the dog never barked. "That was no road-thief," they say. "That was one of ours."
fail_result: Nobody saw anything. Nobody ever does.
You ask, and are told what they would tell anyone: nothing. A door shuts.

text: Four of {gang} step out on the road ahead, not hurrying. "{villain_short} wants to see what you're made of," one says. "Pay the toll, or show us."
The road narrows, and four of {gang} are across it, easy and armed. "The captain sends greetings," one says. "Toll is paid in silver, or in teeth."
A whistle from the trees, and four step out: {gang}, in no hurry. "You're the one who's been asking," says one. "{villain_short} would like a look at you. Pay up, or show us."

label: Show them.
result: "That's what I hoped you'd say," the man says, and draws.
"Good," says one of them. "I was hoping." Steel comes out on all sides.

label: Pay the toll, and remember their faces.
result: They take your silver and stand aside, grinning. You will know them again.
The silver goes into a bag, and the bag goes out of sight. They let you through with a nod, and you note the scar, the limp, the missing finger.

label: Talk your way past them.
result: "Tell your captain," you say, "that I'll be paying my toll at {home}." They laugh, but they let you by.
"Let the captain name the price at {home}," you say. One of them laughs, and then does not, and they stand aside.
fail_result: "Funny," the man says. "Let's see you laugh with your teeth out."
"Clever," says one of them, and the smile goes. "Let's see how clever you are lying in the road."

text: You spend the morning in the yard where the wagons are loaded for the road, and watch who comes to look.
The loading yard smells of tar and mule. You sit on a barrel with a heel of bread and watch the faces, not the wagons.
You pick a corner from which you can see the weighing-post and the gate, and watch who counts the loads, and who counts the counters.

label: Watch who takes too much interest.
result: {outlaw_inside}
It takes the whole morning, and then it is plain. {outlaw_inside}
fail_result: Everyone in {town} takes an interest in the wagons. You learn nothing but the price of salt.
The yard is busy and nobody is out of place. You leave with a sore back and the price of tar.

text: Word comes up from {home} by a boy with a white rag on a stick: {villain} will talk, if you come alone and come soon. {patron} says it is a trap. It may be.
At dusk a boy leaves a message at your door and runs: {villain} will hear your terms at {home}. {patron} says it is a trap. It may well be.

{patron} puts a hand flat on the table. "A word has come down from {home}. {villain_short} will parley. The lord might pardon the gang, if the right person asked. Or you could go up with steel instead. Which is it to be?"

label: Send word back: you will parley.
result: The boy runs off with your answer. You will go up to {home} with your hands open, and your sword loose in its scabbard.
The boy nods and is gone. You have said it now, and a word like that does not come back.

label: Send the boy back with nothing. You are coming to break them.
result: The boy goes back with no answer, which is an answer. {gang} will be waiting.
You give the boy nothing, not even a look, and watch him go. Whatever you bring up to {home} will not be a message.

text: {home} is quiet. A thread of smoke goes up from somewhere inside, and a man on the wall watches you come and does not raise the alarm.
{home} is quiet, and quiet is wrong. A thread of smoke, a horse stamping, and nobody in the way to say stop.
The track to {home} is rutted deep by wagons that were never paid for. At the end of it a lookout leans in a gap and watches you come, and does not call out.

label: Walk in with your hands open, and talk.
result: You talk for an hour by their fire: of the lord's pardon, of the gallows, of what the roads will be in a year. In the end {villain_short} spits in the fire and says, "Done."
You talk until the fire is low: of the lord's pardon, of what a rope costs, of what a clean road is worth. At last {villain_short} says, "Write it, then," and holds out a hand.
fail_result: "No," says {villain_short}, at last, and stands. "I don't think so."
{villain_short} hears you out to the end, politely. Then: "A good speech. You may keep it." The room is very still.

label: Go in by the back way the prisoner told you of.
result: The back way is a goat-path and a gap in the wall, and nobody is watching it.
The prisoner told true: a steep path, a loose stone, a way in that nobody watches.

label: Go in with steel.
result: You draw, and go in.
You do not wait to be asked. Steel is out before the gate is open, and the lookout has barely time to shout.
